Subject: Jurisdictional egress requirements for Acme private VPC

Hi Tessa,

We're moving forward with the private VPC deployment and need to validate a couple of jurisdictional constraints before procurement can sign off. High level asks:

- Confirm whether customer data (request/response payloads and logs) will remain within the EU regional pockets (eu-west-1 / eu-central-1) in normal operation and during failover to APAC.
- Describe any metadata or control-plane traffic that may transit or be stored outside EU/APAC (e.g., US-control plane, telemetry endpoints).
- Provide an egress/lawful access statement we can include in our vendor risk assessment (we've attached our questionnaire).

Can you also confirm whether a warm-standby failover to APAC will result in any customer data egress to a third jurisdiction during the switchover window?

Thanks — procurement team

Attachments: Acme-Security-Questionnaire.pdf (form, 12 pages)
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com
To: procurement@acme-corp.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-06-11T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Jurisdictional egress requirements for Acme private VPC

Hi — thanks for the questions and the questionnaire. Summary answers up front so procurement can proceed:

1) Data locality in normal ops: Customer request/response payloads, long-term logs, and user-provided artifacts will be stored in the customer-dedicated EU data plane (deployed in your chosen EU region) and will not be replicated outside EU unless you enable cross-region replication.

2) Failover behavior (EU -> APAC warm standby): During a warm-standby activation, new session data and incoming requests routed to APAC will be served from the APAC data plane. We will not copy persistent EU-only historical logs to APAC as part of the failover; instead, the APAC environment will maintain its own ephemeral request cache and session store. There is a documented retention policy for any transient caches (see bullet below).

3) Control plane & telemetry: The control plane for Redwood Private uses a customer-managed control-plane option. For standard Private setups (VPC + managed control plane), metadata such as health checks, orchestration events, and usage metrics may be forwarded to a control plane endpoint we host. For Acme, we propose the private control-plane option (customer-managed endpoint inside your VPC) to avoid cross-border telemetry. If you need a SaaS control plane, minimal orchestration metadata may transit our US control plane; we can provide a list of endpoints and attestations.

4) Lawful access/egress statement: We're preparing an attestation document that addresses lawful access handling and jurisdictional egress during failover; see attached summary. We can escalate to an attestation doc for procurement/legal (DocuSign link to follow).

Proposed next steps:
- Tech review call (30m) with Marissa and Karthik to walk the failover sequence diagrams and BGP/NAT behavior.
- Redwood to deliver a signed jurisdictional egress attestation for procurement.

I've attached a short one-page summary for your security team. Happy to expand any section.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com

Subject: Re: Jurisdictional egress requirements for Acme private VPC

Hi all — adding a few technical clarifications from the infra side:

- Networking & peering: For Private VPC deployments we recommend direct VPC peering (or private interconnect) between Acme's VPC and the Redwood private data-plane subnet. We will not establish transitive peering that routes through third-party regions. BGP sessions (if used) are contained within the chosen region's edge and our peering fabric; we can provide ASNs and IP ranges for your firewall team.

- NAT & egress: Outbound egress from the data-plane will be restricted by default. API calls to external services (e.g., SaaS integrations) require explicit allowlists and will be logged. During warm-standby failover, ephemeral outbound flows (health checks, package syncing) from the APAC data plane may hit CDNs in that region only. There is no automatic download of EU customer artifacts to APAC.

- Failover trigger / timeline: Failover is triggered by region health indicators (customizable). Typical failover window for session handoff is 30–90s for routing convergence, plus any application-level session restore. We capture a failover event in audit logs with a timestamp and the routing decision.

- Control-plane isolation option: As Tessa mentioned, the customer-managed control-plane model ensures orchestration metadata remains in your VPC (recommended for Acme). If you choose Redwood-hosted control plane, we will provide a SCIM-2 tokenization and telemetry redaction plan to minimize PII leakage.

Happy to run the 30m tech review. When works for you?

—Marissa
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
